pages.title: Rates
pages.content:
Every stay is priced per room, VAT included, with weekly cleaning and breakfast. A Desk Room is €690 for a week (7 nights) or €2,150 for a month (28 nights); a Window Studio is €890 for a week or €2,790 for a month.

Weekday dinners at the long table are €120 per person per week (Monday to Friday, five dinners). A second guest in the room is €140 per week, breakfast included, without an extra desk.

pages.title: Rooms
pages.content:
Nagare has 24 rooms in the restored boat-builders' lodge: 18 Desk Rooms of 18 m² and 6 Window Studios of 26 m². Every room has a bed, storage, blackout curtains and a kettle.

A Desk Room comes with a fixed desk on the coworking floor; a Window Studio adds its own desk at the lake window. Stays start at seven nights.

pages.title: Coworking floor
pages.content:
The coworking floor has 38 timber desks with 1 Gbps fibre wired at every one, 2 call booths and a meeting room for 8. It is open 24 hours to staying guests and hosted Monday to Friday, 08:30–18:00.

House rules are simple: keep the floor quiet, and take calls in the booths.

pages.title: A week at Nagare
pages.content: Check-in is on Sunday or Monday from 15:00. The week then settles into a routine: breakfast, focused work, a swim or a walk, and a weekday dinner at the long table. Check-out is at 11:00 on the last day.

pages.title: Lakeside
pages.content: Lake Ostra is at the end of the garden: a wooden dock for swimming, boats, a shoreline sauna and a six-kilometre walking loop through the pines. The nearest city is two hours away by train.

pages.title: About
pages.content:
Nagare Workation Hotel opened in 2018 in a restored 1960s boat-builders' lodge on Lake Ostra. Ilse Varga founded it for people who need weeks, not days, to do their best work.

Seven people run it: Ilse Varga (founder and general manager), Daniel Osei (front desk and stays), Mei-Lin Hoang (coworking floor host), Tomás Ferreira (kitchen lead), Ana Petrova (connectivity and IT), Jonas Lindqvist (lake and grounds) and Priya Nair (bookings).

pages.title: FAQ
pages.content: What is the minimum stay? Seven nights. Which days can I arrive? Sunday or Monday, from 15:00. Do I get an invoice? Yes, Priya sends one with every confirmation. Pets are not accepted.

pages.title: Book a stay
pages.content: Choose a week or a month and a room, then send your dates by email to stay@nagare-hotel.example or call +00 46 555 0142. Priya Nair confirms within one working day with an invoice. Arrive Sunday or Monday from 15:00.

pages.title: Contact
pages.content: Nagare Workation Hotel, 12 Shore Road, Ostra. Phone +00 46 555 0142. Email stay@nagare-hotel.example. Front desk daily 07:00–22:00.

posts.title: Four weeks to finish a release
posts.excerpt: Sofia, a product designer, spent a month in a Window Studio to lead a major software release.
posts.content:
Sofia needed uninterrupted focus and dependable connectivity to lead a major software deployment. She booked a Window Studio for a month: a larger room with its own desk at the lake window and a fixed desk on the coworking floor.

Her days followed one routine. Breakfast at eight, the floor opened at 08:30, calls from the booth in the afternoon and a walk on the shoreline loop before dinner. The release shipped in the fourth week.

posts.title: Two translators, one month
posts.excerpt: Karim and Elena translated a dense manuscript in tandem from a Desk Room with a second guest.
posts.content:
Karim and Elena booked a Desk Room for a month with a second guest. They spent four weeks translating a dense manuscript in tandem, pairing shared morning breakfasts with quiet coworking sessions at neighbouring desks.

The printer shelf on the coworking floor got more use than they expected; a printed page, a pencil and the lake window turned out to be the best proofreading setup.

posts.title: A week to write the first chapter
posts.excerpt: Hugo booked seven nights to outline a new book project and set a steady morning writing rhythm.
posts.content:
Hugo is a writer. He booked a Desk Room for seven nights to outline a new book, with breakfast at eight and the desk by the window from nine.

He used the call booth as a quiet room for reading aloud, and the weekday dinner at the long table as the one fixed point in the evening.
